text_fidelity_a:
EZX by EZ Lab EZX-SU361775GY Slim Under The Desk Electric Folding Quiet Anti-Shock Treadmill Hydraulic Armrest Home Office Exercise Body Induction Smart, Gray, 55" x 28.5" x 52" I was hesitant about purchasing this but, I decided to take a risk after seeing comparables online that were more expensive. The treadmill stores easily on the wall and I can move it into place whenever I want to use it. It is easy to control the roll even on a hardwood floor.

For Setup:
1. Place a little lube between the platform and running belt (Oil is included)

For Use:
1. Best to use on a hard surface (Hardwood / Tile)
2. Plug in Treadmill (Fold Handle Up if Needed - Highly suggested for initial use)
3. Stand on the end opposite of the digital readouts
4. Slowly take THREE steps forward (3 dashes stacked up on top of each other will appear on the digital readout)
5. The treadmill will slowly begin to move and continue to increase speed while you walk close to the readout screen
6. To hold a certain speed, walk on the middle section of the treadmill
7. To slow down, walk on the end furthest away from the digital readout
8. Keep in mind the machine will continue to speed up when you walk closest to the digital readout AND it will continue to slow down when you walk furthest from the readout, until it comes to a stop
9. If it comes to a stop and you want to continue your session, step off the treadmill and go back to step 3 of this section

It does take practice to get familiar with the treadmill and how speed adjustments are made. During familiarization, I suggest using the support handle that is on the machine. This is not your typical treadmill that has speed adjustment buttons. Hence, it will take time getting used to how it operates so be careful in the beginning.

For Belt Adjustment:
1. A wrench is included in the box
2. If the running belt tends to slide to the right during use, loosen the adjustment screw on the right side (the screw is on the opposite end of the digital readout)
3. If the running belt tends to slide to the left during use, loosen the adjustment screw on the left
4. Make 1/2 to 1/4 turn adjustments (extreme adjustments can make the tuning process more frustrating)
5. Take your time

I've always unplugged the machine after each use and store it against a wall. The running belt "ran" away from me a couple of times when I first got the treadmill and I prevented my fall by using the handrail. Every time I've had an issue with the speed on the treadmill, it's been due to operator error. I've had to remind myself and be cognizant of the fact that speed adjustments are done differently on this treadmill. I wanted something new, intuitive, easy to store, easy to move, and easy to operate. This treadmill met my criteria and is well designed and built.

I watched a lot of videos online before I purchased it. By the time it arrived, I was familiar with how to use it, what to avoid, and possible safety issues I'd have to keep in mind. I recommend this treadmill for OFFICE USE, WALKING, and LIGHT JOGS. For a workout, I recommend using a traditional treadmill with manual speed & incline adjustments.
text_fidelity_b: EZX by EZ Lab EZX-SU361775GY Slim Under The Desk Electric Folding Quiet Anti-Shock Treadmill Hydraulic Armrest Home Office Exercise Body Induction Smart, Gray, 55" x 28.5" x 52"

text_fidelity_a:
Weslo Cadence G 5.9i Cadence Folding Treadmill, Easy Assembly with Bluetooth, 30-Day iFIT Membership Included So, I ordered this treadmill to get exercise during quarantine. I use to swim in a therapy pool but being its the pandemic the pool has been closed. I need exercise, now. I have gained 25 pounds. I have five months until summer.

So, I asked for my treadmill to be delivered to my condo unit. I asked for them to buzz the door so they can wheel it to my door.

That did not happen that way. I got a message on my phone that it was delivered. I took my two wheeler down to the door just incase I needed it. It was in between two doors. (I am 60 years old and have bad knees)

OMG, the box is huge and extremely heavy. So, first I tried to go through the doorway. It wouldn't fit through, So, I got the pail of salt by the door and pulled that over to hold the door wide open. It took several tries but I got it through.

Then I wheeled it down to my door. It is "HEAVY" (I didn't want to drop it) Then I had to get it through my door. I struggled but I got it up and over the door lip.

I got it to the place I wanted to set it up.

The easy part was removing everything from the box.

There is two things when putting this together that you need another person to help. I didn't have anyone so I used a pillow. because you can't lay it on it's side to attached the base, it will make it uneven.

Turned the TV on and watched some you tube videos. I found 2 good ones. One video showed how to assemble it. The other video was how to use it.

Plus I used some of the comments that people made to Amazon on somethings the manual did not state or I didn't want to look through the manual.

So, I found the on/off switch. It spelled out HELLO, so I than pressed the Bluetooth button for 20 seconds and it's all set to go!

It works fantastically. I love it so far.

text_fidelity_a:
Lixada Camping Stove Wood Burning Stoves Portable Backpacking Stove Stainless Steel Alcohol Stove for Outdoor Camping Hiking Backpacking Picnic BBQ Three flaws and one of them is dangerous!
1. The factory pins fall out, and when lost the stove is useless unless you have something to replace the pins with. This could be a real big problem when your camping or survivalist situation.
FIX: use Bobby pins to replace the factory pins. the ribbed design of the Bobby pins cause a tight feel when slid into the hinges of the stove. When fully assembled it feels very sturdy opposed to using a loose fitting pin that gives the stove a "flimsy feel".
2. The spirit burner plate does not fit any spirit burner I have. My trangia burner gets stuck half way in and scrapes the sides of burner pretty badly. It only needs to be a few centimeters larger, but won't fit the largest brand of spirit burners made (trangia).
FIX: take the sand paper provided with the stove to widen the spirit burner plate. This will allow the trangia burner to fit perfectly
3. THIS IS THE DANGEROUS FLAW
If you place a weighted cup on the top it tends to force the sides outward slightly. This can lead to the spirit burner plate falling down and spilling burning liquid. I used the Stanley field cup, and a few different other stainless cups with the same results. The spirit burner plate needs longer tabs so there is no risk of it falling in anyway shape or form. Each side needs to be 1/4" longer or have bent tabs to lock into place. Burning sticks is about the only purpose this stove has safely..
FIX: buy something safer for liquid fuel burning, otherwise small stick burning only!!
text_fidelity_b: Lixada Camping Stove Wood Burning Stoves Portable Backpacking Stove Stainless Steel Alcohol Stove for Outdoor Camping Hiking Backpacking Picnic BBQ

text_fidelity_a: Hornady 46045 Neck Size Die 30 Cal .308 I purchased this neck sizer die specifically for my outdated RCBS neck sizer die with worn expander ball. Hornady's elliptical expander replicates those used by bench rest shooters as it sizes both on the insert and exit of the case from the die. If you have any irregular shaped case mouth,this expander spindle will straighter out the eccentricity while using. I find it a little time consuming if used for other .30 caliber change-overs such as .308 and 300 Win as you have to dismantle the setting in order to accommodate longer or shorter cases. I'm not a fan of Hornady's "Zip Spindle" system as it requires 3 tools to properly tighten the zip knob or the spindle will slip if the nut is not squeezed tight enough against the interrupted threaded nut. A second necessary wrench absolutely is Hornady's New Dimension red die wrench for this propriatory flatted die lock ring also available from Amazon. I lock the flatted die ring and die into my press,then finally tighten the small zip spindle nut using my Hornady wrench. The new dimension lock rings are great as the tightening screw impinges the 7/8-14 die threads at a tangent to the threads thus not marring the steel threads as most setscrews do. I like this die except for the time consuming zip spindle locking system.

Bare Neckd Ice Cooling Towels for Athletes Sports Fitness Gym Yoga Hiking Travel Hot Flashes| Reusable Wrap Around Ice Pack Suffice to say that I have a medical condition that requires me to not get too hot. Bad things happen and they are very obvious, and not in my head. I can die if I get overheated. I just have to live with it. I also live and often work outside in one of the hottest and most humid parts of the country. Oh, and I'm not rich so I can't just hire people to do my bidding and stay inside all day. The clash of these issues has caused me to try numerous gadgets to stay cool and, honestly, this one works the best (and is one of the cheapest though it could be cheaper).

Chilling vests are ridiculously expensive and marginally effective.

"Snap towels" are a joke. Don't waste your money.

You need something with ice in it, people. And the plastic ice cubes don't work, either, and here's why: real ice melts and makes your shirt cool, too, and lasts LONGER, and is cheap.

So far this towel has worked great. I've used it a dozen times or so in very harsh conditions and bought another as a backup. You buy two dollars worth of bag ice, put it in a cooler, and you have at least two days of continuous personal cooling. The towel is long enough to fit around my big neck.

My niece tried it and told her dad she's never mowing the yard again without one. My daughter has never mowed the yard so I'm still astonished about that on two levels.

So tskile it from someone whose life and vision actually depends on staying cool (I know, sounds crazy, but it is true) : if you live in a HUMID area, this is the best balance of price and cooling you can get.

I am so serious about this product I left without it on me day and drive twenty miles back to get it, then twenty miles back to where I realized I'd forgotten it. Now that's a testimony.
text_fidelity_b: Bare Neckd Ice Cooling Towels for Athletes Sports Fitness Gym Yoga Hiking Travel Hot Flashes| Reusable Wrap Around Ice Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Nordic Walking Poles for Individuals 6’ 2” – 6’ 3” = 132.5cm SWIX of Norway. All 32 Lengths Coming Soon 1-Piece Non-Collapsible. #1 for Hiking, Trekking, Physical Therapy. My review is primarily geared towards people who are interested in learning the Nordic walking techniques and are looking for inexpensive, appropriate walking sticks. It is also a comparison of the sticks offered here and the so-called “crappy Chinese” anti-shock, telescoping sticks. I have purchased both and am including photos below.

I started Nordic walking about 3 or 4 years ago. At the time, I wasn’t sure that this was something I would continue to do and did not want to spend a small fortune on equipment that would, once again, end up unused in a closet. But I was having trouble walking even a short distance (100 ft. or so) without excruciating burning in my legs and back, so thought I needed to give this a shot. I sprang for the cheap sticks and boy, am I glad I did! Within a few weeks, I was walking a mile with very little discomfort. That distance might be laughable to some, but to me, it was a miracle!

But honestly, it had less to do with the type of sticks than it did with learning the proper technique. There are many videos available that demonstrate the technique and anyone interested should spend some time watching them. It is not difficult to learn. In fact once you get the rhythm it’s like riding a bike…you don’t forget how to do it.

As far as the poles go, I see little difference in them. Perhaps at a higher price difference there is, but it’s still more about learning the skills.

Cheap Chinese poles (the black ones in the photos): When I bought mine I made some modifications. The rubber tips that were included wore out quickly. I replaced those with the boot type of tip which has lasted all these years and many miles. The tips are deeply grooved like snow tires and they do pick up small pieces of sand. This will make them slip some on asphalt, but it’s fairly easy to flick a grain of sand out and continue your walk. I also replaced the sponge rubber grip just below the handle (because it tore easily) with some closed cell tubing that I found online. That wasn’t entirely necessary because you never or rarely grab the poles in that area. I should have just eliminated it altogether.

These poles are the twist lock telescoping type (not the clamp type), which is handy when you don’t know what length pole you need in the beginning. But once adjusted, it is a PITA to collapse or readjust them. They do have a scale on them that shows the length you’ve set them to, so if you get these, make a note or find some way of marking the length. I never collapse mine anymore, because I want to start walking immediately, not fiddle with adjustments. However, if you need to pack your walking sticks, and don’t mind messing with the twist locks, this is certainly a consideration when you buy. I have never had the twist locks fail or accidently collapse once snuggly hand tightened.

These poles also have the anti-shock springs. It makes them heavier and, yes, they make a rattling noise every time the pole hits the pavement. Their extra weight does makes their footfall more forceful. I see no advantage to the springs at this point, but I’ve heard that they are helpful when going down steep terrain. Can’t say, because most of my walking is on fairly level pavement. BUT, DO NOT let the noise stop you from buying if you don’t want to spend a lot of money in the beginning. Getting you walking again is far more important than any minor rattles.

The handle grips are very comfortable and include a strap for your hands to go up through. I found these straps were much more comfortable for me and more convenient to use. Just remember to insert your hand up from the bottom of the strap.

Overall, these poles have a bigger diameter than the “real” ones and are slightly heavier. However, I think the few added ounces actually give you a better upper body and arm workout than the lighter poles. So, to me, the extra weight could be advantageous. Cost for these poles was 14.95 for each pole (@29.90). The Leki replacement tips cost $17.31 with tax, and I highly recommend them. I’m not including the rubber grip which is not necessary, so my actual cost was $47.21 with tax.

Real Nordic walking sticks (blue in the photos): As noted above, these are somewhat lighter, thinner, nonadjustable, non-spring-loaded poles. It is important that you order the right length. They adjustable have glove like straps attached to the handle.

Personally, I’m not entirely pleased with these particular straps. As you will see in the photos, their design leaves something to be desired. I have circled the points where they irritate my hands. And here, I will have to make some kind of modification if I want to use these poles for an extended time. The gloves interfere with wearing my fitness watch and the binding on some corners should be more rounded instead of squared off. Strapping your hand in or out, by means of Velcro strips, is awkward; and should you need to let go of your poles if you fall, you’re out of luck. There is a means of length adjustment (by pulling upward on the handle top) which is lacking in the Chinese poles, but it doesn’t solve the rubbing issues, since the part which cradles your hand doesn’t change position. After I have used these poles more, I may try to fashion a strap comparable to the ones on the Chinese poles.

The handles themselves are thinner and (though you shouldn’t be clasping them tightly) may be more suited to smaller hands. I can’t say for sure, but they are still comfortable.

I have a gut feeling that the boot tips on these sticks will wear quickly, needing to be replaced often. However, they do not have the deep tread of the Leki replacement tips and do not pick up grains of rock or sand, so that is an advantage as far as sliding on pavement goes. I will most likely replace these stock tips with the Leki ones and just deal with the rocks.

The cost for these poles (before any changes I may make) is, at this writing, $77.45 including tax and/or shipping. I am, otherwise, perfectly satisfied with these “real” Nordic walking sticks. They are light, not noisy and do what they’re supposed to do.

Both poles need some slight modification, but their functions are identical. Once again, it’s about technique, not one type of pole compared to another. Please do not let any hype make your decision. It’s far more important that you get out there and start walking.
I'm awarding 5 stars to either kind of pole. Both work pretty much equally.

MinnKota Riptide 55 ST Bowmount Trolling Motor with i-Pilot and No Foot Pedal (55lbs Thrust, 54" Shaft) I bought one of these for my 18' Carolina Skiff. I also bought the quick release mount. I bought the quick release mount so I could remove the trolling motor when travelling long distances with the boat. I fish from MD to the Gulf and bouncing down the road wouldn't be be good for it. First impression is that I'm going to like it a lot. I've been in the water twice using the trolling motor, both times in salt water, which is where I spend most of my fishing time. Installation was easy and deploying and retracting the ST55 is also easy. The iPilot anchor function worked well in 1.5 mph currents and 12 knot winds. I'll try it in the 8kt currents in the OBX in August. I like the iPilot control unit and no foot pedal because I'm not restricted to a certain place in the boat. I maxed it out and was surprised at how strong the motor was. I used the motor for about 2 hours and battery drain was about 1.4 volts from 14.2 to 12.8. Totally acceptable, especially for the size boat and winds. The instructions call for a 60 amp inline circuit breaker, however, I'm using a 40 amp and it was fine on full power. I've given it a 4 star rating right now and will return to add more to this review once I've used the programming features of the iPilot.

Update 24 Feb 15: I have nothing but praise for Min-Kota and the RipTide ST55. I've put about 70 hours on this motor and spent many hours in the anchor mode against 2-3 knot tides. I didn't use my boat anchor once during the summer and fall months because the RipTide's anchor function is spot on. I mainly fish in saltwater and I've used it from Florida, to North Carolina, to Maryland and its performance is outstanding. The only down side is it doesn't have automatic deploy and retrieve. I know Min-Kota is working on one. I love the iPilot! I can use it from anywhere on the boat and only have to remember when facing backwards, left is right and right is left. Duh. Most definitely 5 STARS

text_fidelity_a:
Mangrove Pickleball Bag, Men's & Women's Pickleball Backpack, Adjustable Sling Bag with Fence Hook/Upgraded Capacity/Safety Pocket/Water Bottle Holder - 2023 Design Pickle Ball Paddle Bag We recently got a second pickle ball set and needed a bag - so I grabbed this one. I will be honest here: we are not going to get to “use” this for awhile. Just before the pickle ball set arrived my wife severely broke her foot and will be off it for up to 12 weeks. But we love the game and we love how it lets us workout and be in shape, so she/we are determined to get out there and play again!

This bag is great!

First, it’s made of food materials - they feel solid, sturdy, and like they’ll last. The bag looks attractive with its black with white accents. Our other one is blue and we love the look, but the black is sleek and fresh. As I said, the materials are solid and it feels like we’ll get some good, long use out of it. the zippers - always a consideration - are solid, well built, and feel like they’ll last as well. DO NOTE: the middle zipper/section has a looser lining and we noticed the lining tends to come up and risk getting caught - luckily I felt it and stopped before it was an issue. Make sure it lays inside right.

Second, the size of this bag is excellent! We are blown away by how large this bag is, how much it already fits, and how much room remains. Blown away. We have two, covered paddles and 4 balls and there is plenty of room for more. My wife - and I really - think our other 2 paddles would easily fit, as well as another ball or two WITH the 4 paddles - or at the least, a number of extra calls. Keep those out and we could put back up shirts, a light jacket, those types of things in there. Plus there is plenty of room for wallets, keys, and phones.

A bonus is the hook included attached inside. We usually have a carabiner to attach it to something like a fence, or for whatever. This one has the hook, so no need.

Third, ease of carry. This one comes with a strap for over the chest carrying, but no handle - not at a all a big deal. Use the strap or carry it over yourself - as I’ve already done - and make things easy.

Overall this is a great bag and we cannot wait to get back out there and use it! I’m so glad I picked this one and the only bad side... it will taunt us as we wait for my wife to recover... very happy to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Mangrove Pickleball Bag, Men's & Women's Pickleball Backpack, Adjustable Sling Bag with Fence Hook/Upgraded Capacity/Safety Pocket/Water Bottle Holder - 2023 Design Pickle Ball Paddle Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Weslo Cadence G 5.9 Treadmill Series I purchased this less than a month ago. I read reviews on basically every treadmill out there that I could find before purchasing this one. No matter how expensive or in expensive they were I saw that none had a 5 start rating overall. After reading this description and reviews I purchased this model and I am really glad I did! I love this treadmill! I am 5'8" and weight 235 lbs. This treadmill works perfectly with no signs of stress or pressure. It has a good strong motor and the panel is excellent in helping me see how far I walked as well as my heart rate. I have not used the full work out settings yet, (there are 6), but my daughter ran through the cycle of them and they seemed to be very nice. I am working on getting to a full work out as I have a desk job that I work about 12 hours a day so never really did a home or gym work out. Now that my schedule is adjusted it is perfect! I am very happy I bought this product.

Things you should know before you purchase it:

1.It did take 2 people to put it together as adding the bars to the bottom section required someone to hold it in place, but other than that my son was able to do the rest by himself.
2. This is not a light weight machine. So moving it and the parts around you may need help until it is assembled. After that you can simply roll it to the desired location.
3. It is not "compact" or storage friendly. While you can "fold it" to get more space when not in use, you are not going to gain that much space to make a difference. The walking portion of the treadmill folds upward, but not to a straight angle, so it is still slanted, so the storage "area" is still larger than the bars that you hold on to when you walk.

Over all after reading the other reviews and such, I think I did a great job with this purchase. If anything happens over the next few months I will report back, but I don't see any potential issues with this purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Weslo Cadence G 5.9 Treadmill Series

I’m impressed by how the company thought of everything for this safe. Inside the safe is a LED light that automatically is triggered when the safe pops open. The bottom of the safe is lined with a removable piece of foam padding.

If I were have to name something I don’t like about the safe... I appears pretty heavy. But I guess that’s not a bad thing?

text_fidelity_a:
Boat Bow LED Lighting RED & Green Kit Highly recommended! Bright, easy to install, exactly as described, and delivered via usps one day before expected!!!!

I will buy another set in the near future. I lost a little tinkering time because of the below, but they work great and are just exactly what every boat needs! I suggest pulling out that darn pole socket and putting these on! Nothing to break or get lost, and they work like a charm!

Only three small, but note worthy recommendations.

First, the tab on the end if the LED, where the wires join, is not included in the double sided tape. Doesn't take much smarts to realize the end is likely to separate from the boat as a result - just run the double sided tape after you put the end cap together.

Second, there are absolutely no instructions. Granted it isn't brain surgery, but a novice electrician could hook the wires up backwards and presume it is broken.

Third - I also suggest you put some sort of obvious color marking on them. Had to run power to them to confirm which one was which color (red/green). If the were indicators on them I completely missed it.

There are 10 holes/slots for the golf balls to land in with points ranging from 5 to 100. 5 of the 10 balls are white and the other 5 are yellow. Once you decide who goes first he or she will putt all 5 balls toward the base. Anything not in a slot counts as 0 points. After player one shoots player 2 gets to shoot his or her 5 balls. If you're like me, just be prepared to give this plenty of time. That said, this was my first venture into the world of Zumba. I wasn't sure what to expect, other than it was an enthusiastic kind of experience. In case you're like me, it is a very high energy workout. There's basically lots of dancing, and you'll need lots of coordination. There's cultural music that plays in the background, and it was pretty cool, even if the whole package did make me feel old. The people within the videos are all high energy, with big smiles. They made it look so easy!

The good news is even though I haven't been able to do every move(not even close), I can still feel my muscles burning.

Another negative is that fact that these workouts make getting hurt more likely(based on workouts I've done in the past). There's lots of twisting and turning, and there were plenty of times that I could feel unnatural pain, so I'd stop before I did damage. Plus, if you have little ones, there's more danger of getting hurt. In one of the "chair" workouts, during a part where I was standing up, my little came in and turned my chair legs up without me knowing. It hurt when I sat down! ;) (Note: They DO try to warn you about what not to do to hurt yourself in the starting video.)

The videos do range in difficulty, but even the easy ones were pretty tough to keep up with for me. So, again, I wouldn't recommend this as a starting place for beginners. If you're coordinated and like to dance, give this a try!

(This set comes with a pair of 2.5 lb weights. They rattle as you move them. There's also 5 DVD's. It comes with a box that makes it easy to store it all in, and put on a bookshelf when not in use(which is what I do).)
text_fidelity_b: Zumba Fitness Tone Up DVD System

Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer I bought the OMRON HJ-112 pedometer through Amazon.com at $[...]. It's easy to clip on or put in a pocket and has become part of my everyday routine. The LCD display is easy to read and understand. The security strap with a little clip helps keep it from getting lost. I love it and highly recommend it.

The first couple of weeks my wife and I just enjoyed talking about how many steps we had done that day. Then about a week ago I found the "aerobic STEP" display. If you walk 60 steps or more per minute for 10 minutes or more the pedometer displays this as "aerobic" steps. Walking articles suggest 30 minutes a day of "aerobic" walking. With the pedometer you can record an easy pace of 60-80 steps per minute for 30 minutes during a lunch break. Or split it into two sessions of 15 minutes and let the pedometer add them together. The picture I uploaded shows 3396 aerobic steps I did 5 days ago. It took me 34 minutes so that's about 100 steps a minute. For me 100 is a very easy pace to maintain (on level ground, good shoes, etc.) but even a slower 60 a minute is perfectly OK.

So thanks OMRON for adding this much needed activity to my life and helping me measure it. Gadgets are great and this one is highly recommended. $[...] is a real bargain for such proven health benefits.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer

text_fidelity_a: Bearhard Heavy Duty Emergency Blanket, Emergency Tarp, Insulated Blanket, Thermal Waterproof Survival Space Blanket for Hiking, Camping I bought this to use as an emergency blanket for my car. It comes folded up in a thick, Ziplock style clear plastic bag which is also re-useable.  I took it out and unfolded it as soon as it arrived. I wouldn't call it a blanket. Essentially, it's an insulated medium weight tarp.  Would it work as a blanket to keep you warm, dry and protected from the wind, cold, rain, snow, etc.? Absolutely! It folds up very easily and is most definitely re-useable. In its folded form, it takes up about the same amount of space as a small collapsible umbrella and weighs about the same. This will fit very conveniently in the glove compartment or under the seat. I was trying to choose between this and a 100% wool blanket. The wool blanket would be much more comfortable and flexible, but it would also weigh more and take up a lot more space. Additionally, it would cost twice the price, and of course, they're not waterproof. Bearing all that in mind, this will suit my needs just fine. I can always pick up a thin fleece throw blanket for about $5.00 for supplemental warmth and creature comfort.

Mirrycle Incredibell Original Bicycle Bell So far, this is a great bell! I just installed it today after I received it in the mail. It looks and fits great on my 2022 Trek Marlin 6. I was in my garage checking out the new bell and ringing it a few times while my wife was about 40 feet away outside in the driveway talking with her friend who was parked in the driveway with her car running and they both said that they could easily hear the bell. Her friend was in her car and my wife was standing outside the car, mind you, that car was not quite with the cooling fans running and the wind was also blowing to create extra noise. Yes, this bell is plenty loud to get someone's attention. This bell also allows you to rotate the dinger in any position you want, which gives you the ability to position exactly where it is best for you. You just rotate the assembly below the bell and put it how you want it. This is a very well thought out design that works great!

Another example later that evening, I was riding down a pathway that parallels the roadway and as I was approaching a parking lot driveway, there were two vehicles stopped waiting to exit to the roadway. I decided to continue down the pathway between the rear of one vehicle and the front of the other vehicle. But just to make sure that the second car saw me coming, I slowed and chimed the bell three times to get her attention as I was approaching about 25 feet away. She looked up and at me, smiled and waved as I slowly rode between the two vehicles. The bell worked as designed. The construction seems to be sturdy, but time will tell. I would recommend this to anyone looking for a small bell that does the job.
text_fidelity_b: Mirrycle Incredibell Original Bicycle Bell

text_fidelity_a:
OSZLES Portable Badminton Net with Stand Carry Bag, Foldable Volleyball Tennis Badminton Net Rack – Easy Setup for for Outdoor/Indoor Court, Backyard, No Tools or Stakes Required This is a simple, easy to put together, fun on a nice day set.

We decided to try this for perhaps taking to the beach or park and it works great for that type of situation. Adults are going to laugh at the size, but it's also great for kids.

It comes in a small carrying bag. The set is easily pulled out and put together: maybe 3 minutes after your first time. The pieces (arms) will push into one another to form two long lines, with one end attached/hooked together (leave it that way). Then you attach the "bottom" fabric via 4 snaps (2 extras included). Then attach the second end like the first, then the net. It took us maybe 6-8 minutes to figure this out - the instructions are okay to good.

Once up it is small. But it works. We played on our community court. It leaned - enough we used the tube of shuttlecocks we had to "anchor" the one side of the fabric base. This was greatly humorous. text_fidelity_a:
Dynamic Discs Cadet Disc Golf Bag | Introductory Disc Golf Bag | Great for Beginners and Casual Disc Golf Rounds | Lightweight and Durable Frisbee Golf Bag | 10-12 Disc Capacity… My first bag, and I still use it. It holds ten discs easily, although more putters makes it tight (I carry two putters). It is great for those of us who don't want to carry more than 10 discs. The Midnight Blue color looks very nice. The small size of the bag means that it is prone to tipping over on uneven ground, but the discs usually stay put. Because of the lack of other pockets, I typically use the putter pocket for a towel.

The mesh pocket inside the top is unusable when not playing. The height of the discs makes it difficult to close the top, so anything stored in the top will interfere with closing. During play you leave the top unzipped, so you could keep a towel or marker disc in it during the game.

The bottle pocket holds a standard plastic water bottle, but anything bigger is very tight or too big. There is no tie for the beverage holder, so your bottle may fall out if the bag tips over.

Despite these drawbacks, I do recommend this bag for it's small size.

Dynamic Discs: If you come out with a redesign, I'd buy another if it has these improvements. Those of us who prefer to carry fewer discs still need some of the features found on larger bags.
- Ability to hold a larger water bottle would be nice.
- A full-width/full-height pocket for a towel and/or golden disc retriever on the back would be very nice.
- A marker disc pocket on the front of the putter pocket would be nice.
- A small pocket on the opposite end of the bottle holder would be nice.
text_fidelity_b: Dynamic Discs Cadet Disc Golf Bag | Introductory Disc Golf Bag | Great for Beginners and Casual Disc Golf Rounds | Lightweight and Durable Frisbee Golf Bag | 10-12 Disc Capacity…

text_fidelity_a: Stanley GO The Quick Flip GO Bottle 24OZ Glass We have now owned several of these water bottles, as they are a really great size, and we enjoy the flip top feature; however, before purchasing, please know that the plastic lid has a weak point that will break if dropped on basically any surface at all.  While we try very hard not to drop our water bottles, accidents occasionally happen, and the lids of two of our water bottles are now broken.  I was hopeful that I could find replacement lids either on Amazon or on the Stanley website, but, evidently, they do not make replacement lids for these bottles.  I contacted the Stanley company just to make sure that they do not make a replacement lid (I explained that the lids were broken due to drops, and I was hoping to purchase new lids).  I received an email back stating that all Stanley products are covered under a lifetime warrant, and they then asked me to submit pictures and fill out a detailed form, which I did, though, it took me a long time to compile all of the requested information, and I had to resend the email 4 times as their email kept telling me that it was "undeliverable".  A few days later, I received an email saying that my "ticket" had been resolved and closed, but I had never received a response from my original email.  So, I emailed back stating that my issue was not resolved, and I resent all of the information that they had originally requested.  Weeks later, I received an email apologizing for how busy they are and stating that the warranty doesn't cover accidental damage, and that I should look on their website or Amazon for a replacement lid.  So, basically I just wasted a bunch of time submitting useless information that they never needed and never received an answer to my original questions.  So, that's that.  If you buy this water bottle, just know that if it gets dropped at all, the cheap, plastic lid will break, and you will be left with a very nice, but useless water bottle.
text_fidelity_b: Stanley GO The Quick Flip GO Bottle 24OZ Glass

(Water Filter with Water Reservoir) I stayed in my house in 20 degree weather without power for 5 days this past February in Texas and it was at that time that I made myself a promise that I would NOT be caught unprepared again.  I mean, in the intervening months the Texas grid has NOT been updated or fixed in any way so if they are going to leave me in the cold again, I at least will be as prepared as possible.  Not just for cold, but should there be water issues and that's where this water filter comes in.  I mean, if we have no power and the water lines froze and burst, then the water is going to need to be boiled at the very least (I could see a run on grocery stores and the shelves holding water are bare), but if I have a water filter - this one - I can at least feel my water is clean and boiling it will give me double confidence I can drink it.  Definitely something everyone should have in an emergency box, along with matches/lighter, candles, solar radio, hand warmers...several other items, but you get where I'm going with the emergency box.  This gravity water filter is a perfect inclusion in that box.  Would be great for a long hiking trip or just taking on a camping trip just in case.

text_fidelity_a: Master Sportsman Adult 26 Pocket Fishing Vest I have been looking for a vest for my camera equipment.  I got tired of lugging a camera bag around and having to set it down to use the camera.  I was looking at both this vest and the Uncle Milty Travel Vest.  Even though this is listed as a fishing vest I was leaning towards this over the other because of the price since they both had a 4.5 rating.  Because there questions on both vests about sizing I hadn't decided what to do.  Then a last minute deal came up for some travel I had to take.  I couldn't order a vest and get it in time.  I checked the web site for a Dicks Sporting Goods store close to where I live and they had vests in their fishing tackle department.  I went over and found a medium that fit just right.  I'm slender at 140# and 5-8 and have a hard time finding clothes over the internet.  I tried on a small that was more a juvenile size and not adult. The large was too roomy for me.  For people any larger than me a large size would work fine.  The funny thing is the vest I bought is the same exact same one here.  Mine says "Master Sportsman" and not Prestige but looks exactly like this picture.  It was the same price of 24.99.  I used it for my travel and several times since and it is really handy.  I've gotten away for SLRs and use a high end point and shoot camera: Canon PowerShot G12 and a Speedlite 270EXII.  Everything, including batteries and chargers and other stuff, fits in the vest just fine.  While the vest seems heavy when I first put it on I don't notice the weight wearing it.  It is so handy to reach in and get the camera, take some pictures and then slip the camera back in its pocket.  I'll never go back to a camera bag.  I have a small Eddie Bauer hand duffle that I use to carry the vest in.  I just fold the vest in half and roll it up and it fits in the handle duffle just fine.  Because of the weight I use a wooden hanger for the vest to store it on.  I hope the picture shows what everything look like.  It is a really great for around $25.  Enjoy!
text_fidelity_b: Master Sportsman Adult 26 Pocket Fishing Vest

text_fidelity_a:
Paracord 550 Survival Bracelet Gear Straps - Parachute Cord - with Flint Fire Starter, Loud Whistle Buckle and P51 Can Opener. Black and Grey Color with Reflective Pattern I am a firm believer in being prepared for emergencies. I have seen them happen and there have been times that I could have used some equipment to help me through these tough times. I watched a tornado tear through my front yard as a child ad it made me realize how little control we have about disasters and where they will happen. I love that paracord has become a fashion trend because you don't look out of place. The bracelet fits fine and has a whistle, flint and striker on it, but the biggest draw for me was the old fashioned can opener on the bracelet. Most bracelets don't have a can opener, in fact most emergency kits don't come with one, so I'm glad to have one in case of emergency. If you are stuck somewhere and have to eat canned food, it won't help if you can't find a can opener. The paracord can be used for a ton of things, but once you use it the bracelet is done, so save it for a real emergency.

*I RECEIVED THIS PRODUCT AT A DISCOUNTED PRICE (IN ORDER TO TRY IT AND REVIEW) THIS DOES NOT GUARANTEE A GOOD REVIEW, I AM HONEST AND UNBIASED, ALL OPINIONS ON IT ARE MY OWN AND BASED ON THE PRODUCT ITSELF.

text_fidelity_a:
Planet Bike Big Buck front bike fender The inner fork mounting system is ok, but the fender will move around some horizontally not covering all of tire if you are doing any kind of jumping or trail riding.
I modified the fenders, getting rid of the single expansion screw mount. Removed some metal from the mounts, bent them 90 degrees, and both peices of the front fender now bolt horizontally through the Fork hole (where U brakes used to bolt to on the forks). Testing it on my full rigid fat bike, hucking down some dropoffs and over major roots, the fenders now stay perfectly in place.

I left the rear fender unchanged. However, I put on some grip tape on my seat post where the rear fender mounts to by way of strap/cam. Before the grip tape, the rear fender would move slightly side to side. It is now nearly as stable as the front fenders while still allowing quick removal.
text_fidelity_b: Planet Bike Big Buck front bike fender
